- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish after day 15–20, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
